Why "when we have the money" keeps dreams small.

Kevin Trudeau tells of staying at a friend's house when he suggested the group get a private jet. One person replied they would talk about it once they had the money.

Kevin says that is the point, and that it is backwards. Most people let their current means decide what they allow themselves to imagine.

In his view, dreaming big comes first. He calls it one step in his success algorithm.

Do you let your current budget set the size of your dreams?

#ad #mindset #success #money

Two mistakes Kevin keeps seeing in people's dreams.

Kevin Trudeau has talked with people in airports, on planes and in restaurants. He says almost everyone he meets falls into one of two groups.

Some have never dreamed big enough, or at all. Others live in a delusional dream world.

His point is that dreaming is only one of the things you need. You expand the dream, then you set your target.

Which of the two mistakes is easier for you to fall into?

#ad #success #goals #mindset

Why the right attitude has to come before the how.

Kevin Trudeau says people often ask him for the exact strategy or technique. His answer is to forget the how for now, because attitude comes first.

His claim is that without the right attitude, even following the exact same steps will not produce results.

That goes against the usual advice to find the best method first.

Do you think attitude or strategy matters more?

#ad #mindset #success #habits

Ever pulled into the driveway with no memory of driving?

Kevin Trudeau explains a stage called unconscious competence: doing something automatically so you no longer think about it.

He gives two examples. You can drive home while thinking about ten other things, and you can tie your shoelace without being able to explain how.

It shows what it looks like when a skill, or a habit, becomes part of you.

What's one habit you'd like to run on autopilot?

#ad #habits #mindset #success

What Zig Ziglar told Kevin about being born to win.

Kevin Trudeau and Zig Ziglar, the motivational speaker, traveled together for many years. Kevin says Zig told him: you were born to win, engineered for success, designed for accomplishment, and endowed with the seeds of greatness.

The last line was: dream big dreams and don't let anyone steal your dreams.

Kevin chose to leave it there as his closing message.

Which of your dreams deserves more protection?
